executive_summary: Collection window January 25-31, 2028: Paris's Haute Couture Spring/Summer 2028 shows opened within this window, following the close of Fall/Winter 2028 menswear fashion month (2028-01-24), as anticipated in that report. Dior's own site published the house's runway lookbook for its Haute Couture Spring/Summer 2028 show in Paris, and vogue.com independently reviewed the same show, both identifying a bias-cut column dress -- cut on the fabric's diagonal grain so the fabric drapes close to the body rather than falling straight from a vertical seam -- as a recurring construction across multiple looks. This is treated as genuine cross-sector corroboration: one designer_origin source (the house's own lookbook, describing its own runway as designer intent) and one editorial source doing independent runway-review reporting, not a restatement of the house's own materials. Per derive_confidence(), corroboration_count=2 spanning two distinct sectors yields 'high'; this is adopted as computed, applying the same reasoning already applied to the 2028-01-24 Louis Vuitton signal: sector diversity here is genuine (a first-party lookbook plus a separately reported independent review), not a taxonomy artifact (precedent 3) or a mislabeled single underlying source (precedent 7). This remains designer intent (a specific construction shown on one house's couture runway) reported through one designer-origin channel and one independent editorial review; it is not yet a claim of editorial-consensus interpretation across other houses, retail adoption, or social amplification -- couture pieces are made-to-order and not stocked at retail, so no retail-adoption claim is possible or implied for this signal, and none of the other three categories have occurred yet within this window either. No retail, social, resale, independent-criticism, or institutional source introduced a development distinct from this runway coverage this window. The resort 2028 puffer-shell skirt thread, the resale-demand signal on structured waist-tailoring, the obi-sash cocoon coat thread, and the opera-glove/'restraint dressing' thread all produced no new development this window and are not carried forward again absent fresh movement. The Margiela raw-edge thread remains closed out as of 2027-10-18. Met Gala 2027, Wales Bonner, and CFDA's Fashion Fund/Awards remain untracked going forward per standing convention.

top_signals.evidence: Dior published its own runway lookbook for its Haute Couture Spring/Summer 2028 show at Paris Haute Couture Week, and vogue.com independently reviewed the same show, both identifying a column dress cut on the fabric's bias (diagonal) grain -- producing a close, fluid drape against the body rather than the straighter fall of a garment cut on the straight grain -- repeated across multiple looks. The lookbook is the house's own first-party statement of the collection; vogue.com's review adds independent critical framing rather than restating the lookbook's own copy.
